DocumentationNarrative.Body: Command-line tools for BI modeling, conversion, validation, and execution.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the sanctioned BI metadata workspaces.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A BI stack can begin with a source schema, pass through Raw and Business Data Vault structures, continue into a dimensional warehouse, and finish in an analytical target. At each handoff, the next workspace receives declared structure and the evidence needed to bind, generate, deploy, or execute it.
The result is a chain that can be inspected at every boundary instead of one opaque build script.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: How the layers connect

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The AdventureWorks stack composes 27 workspaces and 29 named operations over a live `AdventureWorks2022` source:
- source schema synchronization; - Raw and Business Data Vault and dimensional warehouse creation and deployment; - 53 source-to-Raw, 47 Raw-to-Business, and 20 Business-to-warehouse transforms imported and strictly bound; - three pipelines with modeled cross-pipeline orchestration; - 176 generated Data Quality checks; - portable `MetaAnalytics` projected into `MetaTabular`, then deployed and processed.
A clean run reconciled 31,465 orders, 121,317 order lines, and 163 quota rows from source through the warehouse. It reproduced the expected sales and quota totals and produced zero findings across the promoted Data Quality checks. Repeating the ETL preserved the Raw, Business, and warehouse row totals, and the processed Tabular deployment returned the same analytical values.
Once the stack is created and deployed:
```powershell cd Demos\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo.MetaMesh meta-mesh run --operation run-etl meta-mesh run --operation verify-stack meta-mesh run --operation deploy-tabular meta-mesh run --operation process-tabular ```
The operation names and workspace dependencies are part of the MetaMesh workspace, so the sequence can be inspected and repeated from the model.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: AdventureWorks evidence

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The official BI models divide the stack by ownership:
- `MetaSchema`, `MetaDataType`, and `MetaDataTypeConversion` describe source structures and type mappings. - `MetaRawDataVault`, `MetaBusinessDataVault`, and `MetaDataWarehouse` describe data architecture and physical implementation. - `MetaTransformScript`, `MetaTransformBinding`, `MetaSql`, and `MetaSqlDeployManifest` describe transformation, binding, database objects, and deployment. - `MetaAnalytics` carries portable analytical meaning before a target engine is selected. - `MetaTabular` and `MetaMultiDimensional` describe target-specific analytical models. - `MetaDataQuality`, `MetaPipeline`, and `MetaOrchestration` describe assurance and execution.
`meta-convert` connects these workspaces through explicit model conversions.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: BI model layers

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta-data-quality` turns transform and schema information into generated quality checks and findings.
`meta-pipeline` executes modeled tasks and records the transform, binding, row, batch, timeout, fingerprint, audit, and failure information needed to understand a run. `meta-orchestration` derives dependencies from pipeline tasks and modeled object access, while explicit ordering, synchronization, and failure policy remain part of the orchestration workspace.
Target CLIs deploy or process the analytical workspaces described by the stack.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Execution models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
SQL structure matters to the BI layers that depend on it.
`MetaTransformScript` imports supported SQL into a typed syntax model and can emit equivalent SQL. `MetaTransformBinding` checks that modeled reads and writes resolve against source and target `MetaSchema` workspaces and follow the selected `MetaDataTypeConversion` policy. `MetaSql` and `MetaSqlDeployManifest` carry deployable database structure and controlled deployment.
The result is a chain of declared contracts rather than independent tools guessing from SQL text.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: SQL structure and binding

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta-bi` is the BI modeling layer built on `meta`. It carries source contracts through SQL transformation, Data Vault, warehouse, quality, pipeline, orchestration, and analytical target workspaces. Each handoff remains a workspace that can be reviewed, converted, deployed, or executed.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the core metadata foundation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta` organizes commands by the work performed on a workspace:
- **Create:** create an empty workspace or project an existing workspace onto another surface. - **Inspect:** view workspace status, models, instances, relationships, queries, and graphs. - **Author:** add or change model definitions and instance records. - **Refactor:** change model structure together with the affected instance data. - **Import and export:** bring external metadata into a workspace or write it in another supported form.
Workspace-oriented commands use the current directory by default. Pass `--workspace <path>` to target another workspace. Use `meta help` for the command list and `meta help <command>` for the current arguments and options; the complete command reference is generated from that same modeled command surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Meta CLI at a glance

DocumentationNarrative.Body: - [XML workspace contract](https://metametabi.com/docs.html#subject-public-meta-xml-workspaces) specifies the XML model and instance formats. - [Meta CLI reference](https://metametabi.com/docs.html#group-public-meta-cli) is generated from the modeled command surfaces. - [Meta model reference](https://metametabi.com/docs.html#group-public-meta-models) describes the foundation models. - [Development package documentation](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta/blob/master/PACKAGE-README.md) records the maintained package boundaries. - [Contributor guidance](https://github.com/jimmy-zhao-tainio/meta/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers repository builds and generated-artifact policy.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Further reference

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Create an XML workspace and give its initial model one entity and two records:
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --xml meta model rename-model MetadataModel WorkspaceCatalog --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta model add-entity System --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta model add-property System SystemName --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta insert System erp --set SystemName=ERP --workspace .\XmlWorkspace meta insert System crm --set SystemName=CRM --workspace .\XmlWorkspace ```
Now create SQL and C# workspaces from that exact model and instance graph:
```powershell $env:META_SQL_CONNECTION = "Server=.;Database=WorkspaceCatalog;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;Encrypt=false" meta create --new-workspace .\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --connection-env META_SQL_CONNECTION --sql meta create --new-workspace .\CSharpWorkspace --source-workspace .\XmlWorkspace --with-instances --csharp ```
The C# surface contains the generated `WorkspaceCatalogModel`, the `System` type, and the same two records. Application or service code can consume them directly:
```csharp using WorkspaceCatalog;
WorkspaceCatalogModel catalog = WorkspaceCatalogInstance.BuiltIn; foreach (var system in catalog.SystemList) { Console.WriteLine($"{system.Id}: {system.SystemName}"); } ```
All three workspaces carry the `WorkspaceCatalog` model, its `System` entity, and the `erp` and `crm` instances. Only their storage and execution surfaces differ.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: One workspace across XML, SQL and C#

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Metadata is the structure that tools operate on. A model defines entity types, scalar properties, and relationships. Its instance graph contains identified records and references. A workspace carries both so the same declared meaning can be authored, inspected, changed, and moved between surfaces.
Core terms:
- **Model:** a named set of entity definitions. - **Entity:** a record type with an identity. - **Property:** a scalar value on an entity. - **Relationship:** a reference from one entity to another. - **Instance:** one identified record of an entity. - **Workspace:** the unit that carries a model, its instance graph, and the selected surface.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Metadata foundations

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The repository targets .NET 8. Build the foundation from its root:
```powershell dotnet build Metadata.Framework.sln ```
Run the CLI directly during development:
```powershell dotnet run --project Meta\Cli\Meta.Cli.csproj -- help ```
For an offline release, extract the archive without changing its layout and run `install-meta.exe`. A framework-dependent package requires the .NET 8 runtime; a self-contained package carries its runtime. The installer places `meta.exe`, `meta-weave.exe`, and `meta-docs.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\meta\bin` and adds that directory to the user `PATH`. Open a new terminal, then run `meta help`.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Install and run

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A supported surface is isomorphic when it can carry the modeled facts of a workspace without assigning them a different meaning. The model, identities, scalar values, and relationships remain the same when the workspace moves between XML, SQL, and C#.
- **XML** stores deterministic model and instance files. Their structured, stable ordering makes metadata changes practical to review, branch, merge, and version in Git. - **SQL** stores the workspace in relational tables, where database constraints, queries, and set-based operations can work over large instance sets. - **C#** stores readable and writable typed source for applications and services that need to consume or produce the workspace directly.
Commands open the selected surface through the common workspace contract, apply operations to the same modeled state, and persist through that surface or a selected destination surface. XML is not a canonical semantic form; it is one first-class representation alongside SQL and C#.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Why isomorphic metadata

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Five command-line tools share the foundation:
- **`meta`** creates and operates on model and instance workspaces across XML, SQL, and C# surfaces. - **`meta-cli`** defines modeled command surfaces and provides shared parsing, help, workspace access, and runtime binding. - **`meta-weave`** authors and validates declarative correspondence between source and target workspace contracts. - **`meta-docs`** combines CLI and model reference data with authored technical documentation, then merges and renders the public reference. - **`meta-mesh`** declares the workspaces involved in a repository workflow and the ordered executable steps that operate on them.
BI-specific models and command-line tools live in the separate `meta-bi` repository.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Foundation command-line tools

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta` is a model-first metadata foundation. It lets tools and people create, inspect, change, and move one workspace contract across XML, SQL, and C# without making any one representation the source of semantic truth.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A workspace contains one model, one instance graph, and the storage required by its selected surface. Commands address the workspace as a unit rather than depending on a particular file, table, or generated type.
The line-oriented `workspace.meta` descriptor selects the surface with `representation xml`, `representation sql`, or `representation csharp`. A SQL workspace also names the environment variable that supplies its database connection. XML files, SQL tables, and C# source remain owned by their respective surfaces behind this common boundary.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Workspace contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`instances/*.xml` stores the records for an XML workspace. The root element names the model, and each entity is grouped under its deterministic list container.
For the small fictional `WorkspaceCatalog` model:
```xml <WorkspaceCatalog> <SystemList> <System Id="erp"> <SystemName>ERP</SystemName> </System> </SystemList> </WorkspaceCatalog> ```
Every record has an `Id`. Scalar properties are child elements; relationships are stored as `...Id` attributes. Missing elements mean that an optional value is unset.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Instance XML contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`model.xml` declares which entities exist, which scalar properties they carry, and how they relate.
A model has one `<Model name="WorkspaceCatalog">` root and follows a small set of rules:
- `<Entity name="System">` defines a record type; every entity has an implicit `Id`. - `<PropertyList>` contains scalar fields. Properties are required by default; `isRequired="false"` makes one optional. - `<RelationshipList>` contains references to other entities. Relationships are required by default. - A relationship role distinguishes multiple relationships to the same target entity. - Entity instances are grouped under deterministic `<EntityName>List` containers.
The XML model contract keeps structure explicit and reviewable without making XML the canonical semantic representation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Model XML contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body: The XML surface stores a workspace as a line-oriented `workspace.meta` descriptor, one `model.xml`, and deterministic instance files under `instances/`. This reference specifies that representation; it does not assign XML a privileged semantic role.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: XML workspaces
